title: Done Means Visible — Stages Are Not Destinations

intelligence.essence: A thing is done when the person it is for can see it working — not when it is built, merged, or announced. Work has three stages: BUILT (exists somewhere), LANDED (on main), LIVE (visible at the real address, clicked by the filer, card standing in the feed) — and done means LIVE only, never borrowing the next stage's evidence. The same honesty runs upstream: ten-star service does the work at the earliest moment the system knows it will be needed, so by the time a person reaches for a thing it is already there, rendered and waiting. And delivered means understood: elite from the first version, composed from inventoried parts, in a form a person can actually take in.
intelligence.human_view: "Done" used to mean "I built it and told someone." These notes move the finish line to where it always should have been: the moment the person it was made for can see it working. Everything upstream of that is a stage — real, sometimes hard, but not the destination, and never reported as if it were.
intelligence.child_view: You haven't finished tidying your room when the toys are in a pile by the door. You've finished when someone walks in and sees a tidy room. And the kindest helpers set the table before anyone sits down — so when you arrive, everything is already there waiting for you.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's the difference between "the cake is in the oven" and "the cake is on the table." We learned to say which one is true. And a good host doesn't start cooking when the guests sit down — the meal is ready when they arrive, because somebody thought ahead.
intelligence.ai_view: Report the stage you are actually at, in its own name: BUILT, LANDED, or LIVE. Before you share any link, click it yourself and see your title. Spot value and file it in the same pass — no order required. When you build anything a user will touch, find the earliest upstream trigger and precompute there; a read that starts work is a design smell. Check your Created stamp and your IB filename before you land; the feed sorts and the share machinery keys off them. Receipts out: commit, file SHA, live title, feed position, the exact tap.
intelligence.what_it_means: Visibility is the contract between a system and the people it serves: until the work appears where they live, it does not exist for them — and a system that reports stages as destinations will slowly stop knowing what is real. Pairing that honesty with proactive production is the whole of ten-star service: the work done early, the truth told exactly.
whats_inside: Done = LIVE: visible at the real address, clicked by the filer, standing in the feed at the position its date earns.
Stages are reported as stages; borrowing the next stage's evidence is a defect, not optimism.
Service is proactive by architecture: precompute at the earliest upstream trigger, serve reads from rest.
Quality is part of done: elite-only, inventoried parts, understandable — a visible-but-below-standard delivery is not done either.
Small canonical details (the Created stamp, the IB filename) are load-bearing, not clerical.
